chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: Travelling with the World's Greatest Jazz Band and Duke's schedule
summary: He compares the World's Greatest Jazz Band's travelling with Duke Ellington's and discusses Billy Butterfield's bus rides and Harry Carney.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, he certainly was a traveler.
Oh yeah. So was The World's Greatest Jazz Band! Well, they didn't travel as extensively as Duke, but they traveled extensively over the United States.
Yeah, Billy Butterfield told me about some of those bus rides. It's unbelievable.

It's amazing how some guys could make that all their...you know, practically all their lives. That's for instance what Harry did. Of course, he... Duke always rode with him, so that was different circumstances. But even so, all that traveling; it's incredible.
I don't know how they(?) (?)held up(?) under all that traveling.

Well, I think he... I know he loved Duke very much. He sort of knew that he was helping him. As much as he was featured in the band, I always felt that I wanted to hear him more. He made a beautiful album that Strayhorn wrote, when he plays like "Moonlight On The Ganges."
